land.text: the left bank of the Dniester, then part of the Moldavian SSR, which the 2 September 1990 congress proclaimed a separate republic; six 15 km circles on the river intersected with Moldova, 14 grid cells (about 3,542 km2)

predecessors.note: The Transnistria infobox reads 'Independence from Moldavian SSR declared: 2 September 1990', so the land is the Moldavian SSR's (the Soviet Union stayed the sovereign: Gorbachev annulled the proclamation on 22 December 1990 but 'little was done to enforce the decree'). Redrawn after review: the first version was one grid cell.

capitals.name: Tiraspol
capitals.note: 'Tiraspol is the capital and largest city.' Coordinates are the city's.

correction.text: the left bank of the Dniester from Camenca to Slobozia, drawn as six 15 km circles on the river (Camenca, Rîbnița, Cocieri, Grigoriopol, Tiraspol, Slobozia) intersected with Moldova: 14 grid cells, about 3,542 km2 (infobox 4,163 km2); the cell that holds Tiraspol also holds Bender, so Bender cannot be left out at this resolution

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, redrawn after review (the first version, Natural Earth's one-cell 'Transnistria' unit of 253 km2, was about one fifteenth of the strip). The page gives no area for 1990-91; the infobox 'Total: 4,163 km2' (no year) is for today, and the 1924 ASSR 'included today's Transnistria (4,100 km2)'. Measured with the gazetteer: this shape resolves to 14 cells, about 3,542 km2, ratio 0.85 to the infobox (within a factor of two). The strip is narrower than a cell, so the cells on the river straddle both banks, and H3 cell 851e5c8bfffffff holds both Tiraspol and Bender: the 1992 gain of Bender adds no cell. The page does not say whether Bender or the right-bank villages were claimed in 1990-91 (it says only that the PMR 'claims' Varnița, Copanca and the Dubăsari-area villages, no date).

union.text: the left bank of the Dniester from Camenca to Slobozia, drawn as six 15 km circles on the river (Camenca, Rîbnița, Cocieri, Grigoriopol, Tiraspol, Slobozia) intersected with Moldova: 14 grid cells, about 3,542 km2 (infobox 4,163 km2)

correction.text: the left (eastern) bank of the Dniester in the PMR's reading, with Bender (Tighina) and four right-bank communes; the left-bank part is six 15 km circles on the river intersected with Moldova, Natural Earth's Bender unit added; 14 grid cells, about 3,542 km2 (infobox 4,163 km2)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, redrawn after review (the first version, Natural Earth's one-cell 'Transnistria' unit plus Bender, was 5 cells, about 1,265 km2, ratio 0.30 to the infobox, and left out the northern left bank from Rîbnița and Camenca; the note then wrongly said 'within a factor of two'). Measured with the gazetteer: this shape resolves to 14 cells, about 3,542 km2, ratio 0.85 to the infobox 'Total: 4,163 km2' (no year on the page); it is the same 14 cells as the 1990-91 shape because Bender shares a cell with Tiraspol. The page: 'The territory controlled by the PMR is mostly, but not completely, conterminous with the left (eastern) bank of Dniester'; the PMR controls 'the city of Bender (Tighina) and four communes' on the west bank, and 'Six communes on the left bank' stayed under Moldovan control; the shape cuts out neither. Natural Earth's Bender unit is four cells (Bender, Tiraspol and the southern left bank), so it is wider than the city.

region.text: Transnistria, the left bank of the Dniester (six 15 km circles on the river intersected with Moldova, 14 grid cells)

ledger.note: 2 September 1990: Transnistria proclaims itself a separate republic. 'An ad hoc assembly proclaimed the Pridnestrovian Moldavian Soviet Socialist Republic (PMSSR) after a referendum' on 2 September 1990; Gorbachev annulled it on 22 December 1990. The page names the region, not its boundary. The land was the Moldavian SSR's (infobox: 'Independence from Moldavian SSR declared: 2 September 1990'), hence that counterpart; the republic-of-moldova row begins in 1992.

5 November 1991: the republic drops its Soviet label. It 'dropped its Soviet association and was renamed the Pridnestrovian Moldavian Republic'; the infobox dates a declaration of independence from the Soviet Union to 25 August 1991.

region.text: the Dubăsari area, where the Cocieri and Coșnița bridgeheads were seized in March 1992, and Bender, fought over 19-21 June 1992

ledger.note: 2 March 1992: the Transnistria War begins. 'Fighting intensified on 1 March 1992'; on 2 March Cocieri locals seized an arms depot at Dubăsari, trench warfare followed, and a second bridgehead formed at Coșnița on 13 March. Earlier clashes (2 November 1990 at Lunga, 13 December 1991) held no ground.

region.text: the Dubăsari area, where the Cocieri and Coșnița bridgeheads were seized in March 1992, and Bender, fought over 19-21 June 1992

ledger.note: 21 July 1992: Yeltsin and Snegur sign the ceasefire. 'A ceasefire agreement, signed on 21 July 1992, has held to the present day' (Transnistria page); the 14th Army's artillery strike of 3 July 'effectively' ended the fighting around Bender, after the Battle of Bender of 19-21 June. The ceasefire set up a Joint Control Commission and a joint force of five Russian, three Moldovan and two PMR battalions.

region.text: Bender (Tighina) on the west bank, with its four communes; a 6 km circle on the city (Natural Earth's Bender unit is four cells and takes in Tiraspol)

ledger.note: 1992: the PMR keeps Bender. The PMR 'also controls Bender (Tighina) and several nearby villages on the west bank, which lie outside Transnistria as Moldova defines it'; the war page says PMR forces and the 14th Army drove the Moldovan army out of the city but gives no territorial tally, so the month follows the ceasefire. At the grid's resolution Bender and Tiraspol are one cell (851e5c8bfffffff), already in the 1990-91 shape, so the gain adds no cell.

wars.name: Transnistria War

zones.text: the Dubăsari area, where the Cocieri and Coșnița bridgeheads were seized in March 1992, and Bender, fought over 19-21 June 1992

wars.outcome: Transnistria became de facto independent but remained internationally recognised as part of Moldova; ceasefire of 21 July 1992 with a Joint Control Commission and a mixed peacekeeping force; nearly 1,000 dead.
wars.note: Russia's 14th Army (the Soviet 14th Guards Army until April 1995, then the Operational Group of Russian Forces) 'supported the separatists throughout'; the Transnistria page's infobox dates the war 2 March to 1 July 1992 and the ceasefire 21 July. Russia is listed as the Russian Federation (Cliopatria row from 1992).

certainty.note: Boundary of the proclaimed republic undefined on the pages.
A ceasefire line, not a recognised border; Moldova's special status law of 22 July 2005 excludes Bender and the Moldovan-held areas; the pages give no coordinates.

sources.title: Transnistria
sources.note: Declarations 1990-91, area 4,163 km2, Bender, security zone, Russian troops, recognition, 2024-25 events, 2005 law. Re-read 2026-10-31 for the review fix: 'mostly, but not completely, conterminous with the left (eastern) bank', Bender and four communes on the west bank, six left-bank communes under Moldovan control, five raions and the city of Tiraspol.

sources.title: Transnistria War
sources.note: Phases of the war 2 March to 21 July 1992, Bender 19-21 June, Dubăsari bridgeheads.

notes: A de facto state Cliopatria lacks as a row of its own (its 'Russian-occupied territories' row, 1992-2024, 7,000 km2, lists Moldova among its countries and is another eu-22 part's; whether it contains Transnistria is that author's call). The end year 2026 is the project's last year, not an end. Not settled: the PMR's exact boundary (only 'mostly, but not entirely, on the left bank'), the Moldovan-held eastern-bank localities, the date of the PMR's control of Bender before 1992, the leaders' terms (the pages give none for Smirnov, Shevchuk or Krasnoselsky, so there is no ruler strip), the 2006 referendum (97.2% for 'independence from Moldova and free association with Russia', unrecognised) and the Russian troop level. The occupation label for the Russian forces is political and was left out. The 25 August 1991 independence declaration is the infobox's only. The 4 September 2024 ban on the term 'Transnistria' and the 2024-25 energy crisis are on the page. Gazetteer: 'Bender' and 'Transnistria' are Natural Earth admin1 names; Cocieri and Coșnița are not in places. Redrawn after the review (2026-10-31): both keyframes are now the left bank as six 15 km circles on the Dniester intersected with Moldova, 14 cells (about 3,542 km2, ratio 0.85 to the infobox 4,163 km2), Natural Earth's Bender unit added in 1992; the first drawing (5 cells, ratio 0.30) missed the northern left bank. At 253 km2 a cell is wider than the strip, so cells on the river straddle both banks, and Tiraspol and Bender share a cell. The 1990 counterpart is now the Moldavian SSR dossier.
